newsitem.title: USA: US CREDIT OUTLOOK - Jobless claims rise expected.
newsitem.headline: US CREDIT OUTLOOK - Jobless claims rise expected.

text.p: The weekly U.S. jobless claims report is the only scheduled event that could affect U.S. government securities trading on Thursday and it could be mildly positive for bond prices, analysts said.
Economists polled by Reuters forecast, on average, that new claims for state unemployment insurance rose to 341,000 in the week ended July 5 from 332,000 new claims a week earlier.
A rise in claims could reinforce the bond market's uptrend as it might encourage the notion that the labor market is not getting tighter, analysts said.

James Glassman, senior economist at Chase Securities Inc., estimates that new jobless claims rose to 350,000 in the week ended July 5 due largely to a widespread shutdown in the auto industry when factories are retooled to produce new models.
"The shutdowns are due to model changeovers and the industry has concentrated a lot of these shutdowns in the early July period," he said.
Glassman said auto parts suppliers are also affected by such shutdowns and some of their employees might have filed for unemployment insurance during the period.
Once the market absorbs the data in the 0830 EDT/1230 GMT jobless claims report, it will have little to guide it but the positive technicals and sentiment that have aided it all week.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond ended near session highs on Wednesday, up 10/32 to 100-28/32 and yielding 6.56 percent.

Anticipation of a friendly June Producer Price Index (PPI) report on Friday could be constructive for the market on Thursday. But some participants might also choose to take some profits ahead of the report, figuring that any positive impact might already have been discounted, analysts said.
